zh.title: 一颗正在运转的家园
zh.intro: 阳光送来能量，海水搬运热量，岩石与大气也在改变。沿着同一条线索，看看地球怎样为生命提供条件。
zh.more: 深入：机制、证据与模型边界

water.question: 冷水一定沉下去吗？还要看看盐分。
water.hint: 改变 A 的温度和盐度，再播放分层。B 保持 15°C、SP 34。冷而较淡的海水也可能更轻。
water.diagram: 固定剖面中的两份连续海水。A 由暖棕圆点追踪，B 由浅色菱形追踪；同一组标记随密度关系作可逆的几何重排，不是流体动力学解。
water.reference: B 始终是 15°C、盐度 SP 34；比较时体积相同、压力相同。
water.saltNote: 这里的“较淡”仍是海水。SP 是实用盐度；35 大致对应每千克海水含 35 克盐，并非精确换算。
water.difference: A 减 B 的密度差
water.progressNote: 播放只在七个显示秒内展开相对位置，可暂停、回退；不是实际流场或速度。圆点和菱形追踪同两份水，不是分子，也不模拟热盐扩散。
water.rise: A 更轻，倾向停留在 B 上方。试着让 A 变冷：盐分较少时，它也可能仍然更轻。
water.sink: A 更密，倾向下沉到 B 下方。冷却与增盐可以共同增加海水的密度。
water.neutral: A、B 的密度在当前显示精度内接近；这里不画出明确的密度分层。
water.globalTitle: 为什么全球海流不只是一条传送带？
water.globalIntro: 局部密度差能使水下沉，却不能独自解释全球海流。沿着箭头找出表层、深层和返回表层的不同途径。
water.globalDiagram: 相连大洋的机制示意：表层风驱环流、部分高纬海域下沉、深层多分支交换以及风与混合帮助水返回上层。
water.surface: 表层：风推动、地球自转影响方向
water.deep: 深层：较密海水的下沉与交换
water.return: 返回上层：风驱上升与混合
water.globalNote: 自绘机制图，不是实时海流、精确航线或速度预测；大洋并非只有一条“传送带”。
water.bridge: 局部密度差只是海流的一部分。还可以继续观察大气、昼夜或地球上的其他相连问题。
water.deepTitle: 相同体积，为什么质量不同？
water.deepText: 密度是单位体积的质量。在这里的海水范围内，降温通常使密度增加，增盐也使密度增加。两种作用可能加强，也可能抵消。真实水柱还受压力、混合、风和地形影响；少量淡水的低温反常不在这组控制范围内。
water.model: 读数采用 EOS-80 的表面压力状态方程，输入范围为 5–25°C、SP 30–38，显示至 0.1 kg/m³。它是有限的教学比较；现代海洋学采用 TEOS-10。示意位置不由流体动力学求解，也不模拟热盐扩散；密度差小于 0.05 kg/m³ 时归入显示分辨率带。
water.sectionNote: 固定剖面 · 颜色和符号追踪来源；虚线不是隔板，也不表示真实水色或温度。

sky.question: 同一颗地球：昼夜为什么变，极光又为什么亮？
sky.hint: 拖动太阳时，跟着赤道站点 EQ-A 走一圈；再逐层看太阳风、磁场与极光。
sky.timeNote: 北极上空俯视；春秋分情景、固定赤道站点。太阳时不是当地民用时钟；忽略大气折射和晨昏微光。
sky.daynightDiagram: 从北极上空俯视的昼夜示意。阳光从左照来，EQ-A 沿赤道绕地球转动。
sky.daynightTitle: 地球尺度 · 自转与光照
sky.spaceTitle: 近地空间尺度 · 粒子与磁场
sky.spaceDiagram: 近地空间剖面机制示意，磁层在向阳侧受压，在背阳侧拉成长尾；高能粒子沿磁场进入极区上层大气，产生极光。
sky.layerNote: 这些开关只显示或隐藏解释图层，不是在关闭太阳风、地球磁场或大气。
sky.scale: 两图视角不同；地球、磁层、极光层厚度不共用比例尺。
sky.explain: 自转使站点轮流朝向和背向太阳，形成昼夜。极光走的是另一条因果链：太阳风与磁层耦合，粒子获得能量并进入极区上层大气，碰撞使气体发光。
sky.dayAurora: 极光也会在白天发生；暗天空让可见光极光更容易看见。晨昏线不会制造极光，赤道站点也不是极光观测点。
sky.bridge: 光照、海洋和太空环境各有机制。它们一起作用时，能不能用一个开关判断地球适不适合生命？
sky.deepTitle: 光子与带电粒子，不是同一股“风”
sky.deepText: 阳光携带辐射能，太阳风是等离子体流。地球磁场能改变带电粒子的路径；它不是挡住所有辐射的硬壳。部分粒子和能量仍能进入磁层，磁层中被加速的粒子可激发上层大气。这里画的是机制位置，不是当前空间天气或极光预报。

conditions.question: 如果改变一个条件，能推断到哪里？
conditions.hint: 从能量进入，到大气与海水，再到长期变化：每个问题都分清“有依据的方向”和“还缺的条件”。
conditions.distance: 日距 r（今天平均日距 = 1 AU）
conditions.irradiance: 大气外、正对太阳的单位面积日照
conditions.formula: 相对日照 = 1/r²。保持太阳光度不变，只比较大气外正对阳光的单位面积；不是地表温度，也不是宜居判据。
conditions.diagram: 参考日照与改变日距后日照的等比例柱形比较，基准为一。
conditions.thread: 收到多少能量 → 大气保存与海洋搬运 → 引力、岩石和卫星影响长期演变
conditions.closing: 生命的家园不是凑齐几个打勾条件。距离、大气、海洋、岩石和恒星活动互相影响；我们在这里比较机制，不给地球打“宜居分”。

orbit.name: 日距与能量
orbit.ask: 如果地球离太阳近 5%，海洋就一定蒸发光吗？
orbit.robust: 同一太阳下，距离变为 0.95 AU，单位面积接收的日照约增加 10.8%。
orbit.unknown: 仅凭这一步，不能算出升温多少或所有海洋是否蒸发。还需要云、冰的反射率，大气温室作用，海洋热量储存与输送，以及持续时间。
orbit.evidence: 光向外传播时分布到越来越大的面积；日照随距离平方的倒数变化。气候对能量变化的响应还包含反馈。
orbit.connection: 海水页改变的是局部温盐；这里改变的是能量输入，不能直接把滑块换成全球海温。

atmosphere.name: 大气与保温
atmosphere.ask: 如果温室作用较弱，白天地球还会接到阳光吗？
chain: 温室气体吸收并再发射
atmosphere.robust: 阳光仍能送来能量。在其他条件相同的比较中，较弱的温室作用会使地表较冷；保温作用日夜都存在。
atmosphere.unknown: 不能用“大气有或无”一个开关算温度。气体成分、压力、云和水汽都会改变能量收支；自然温室效应也不等于越强越好。
atmosphere.evidence: NASA 的能量收支与温室效应资料区分入射阳光和向外的热辐射；水汽还会随温度变化形成反馈。
atmosphere.connection: 昼夜图只回答站点是否照到太阳；夜晚不会让温室作用停止。

gravity.name: 质量与引力
gravity.ask: 如果质量少 20%，地球会很快失去水吗？
gravity.robust: 若暂时保持半径不变，质量减小会削弱表面引力。引力影响大气粒子逃离所需的能量。
gravity.unknown: “少 20%”本身不能给出失水速度。还须说明半径、大气成分与温度、太阳紫外辐射、补给和地质历史。改变质量也未必能保持半径不变。
gravity.evidence: ESA 的火星与金星比较显示，引力和太阳紫外辐射共同影响离子逃逸；不能把两颗行星的差别都归到磁场。
gravity.connection: 密度、质量、体积有联系；海水密度的局部对照并不是行星大气逃逸模型。

interior.name: 内热与岩石循环
interior.ask: 如果地球内部逐渐冷却，明天就会失去海洋吗？
interior.robust: 内热参与驱动板块运动和火山活动。岩石、海洋和大气之间的物质交换影响长期环境。
interior.unknown: 不能从内热减少直接推出明天的气温或海洋消失时间。岩石圈演化涉及漫长时间，也没有在这里证明板块构造是所有生命的必要条件。
interior.evidence: USGS 区分地球形成时留下的热与放射性衰变供热；火山直接释放的热远小于太阳输入，岩石循环还有长期碳交换。
interior.connection: 海流搬运已有的热量；内热推动的岩石变化属于另一套时间尺度。

moon.name: 月球与长期变化
moon.ask: 如果没有月球，地球就一定不能住吗？
moon.robust: 月球参与造成潮汐，并约束地球自转轴倾角的长期变化。
moon.unknown: 不能据此判定所有无月行星都不宜居。无月地球的倾角演化还取决于初始自转与其他行星扰动；研究中的不同设定会得到不同变化范围。
moon.evidence: NASA 的地球资料介绍月球对轴倾角的作用；NASA 收录的无月地球数值研究检验了多种初始条件。它们不是把月球突然删除后的实验记录。
moon.connection: 昼夜由地球自转形成；月球并不是每天把地球的黑夜遮出来。

magnetic.name: 磁场与太空环境
magnetic.ask: 如果没有全球内禀磁场，大气就会被剥光吗？
magnetic.robust: 地球磁场改变太阳风带电粒子的路径，也参与极光和部分逃逸过程。
magnetic.unknown: 磁场不是大气的开关。金星没有类似地球的全球内禀磁场，却保有浓厚大气；引力、紫外加热、成分、补给与历史也要考虑。
magnetic.evidence: ESA 对地球、火星和金星的比较显示，磁屏蔽与大气保留并非一对一关系；电离层也能与太阳风形成感应磁层。
magnetic.connection: 天空页隐藏磁场图层只改变画法；不能拿它当作移除磁场后大气损失的模拟。

en.title: A home that keeps working
en.intro: Sunlight brings energy, seawater carries heat, and rocks and air keep changing. Follow one thread to explore the conditions Earth provides for life.
en.more: Go deeper: mechanisms, evidence and limits

water.question: Does cold water always sink? Check its salt, too.
water.hint: Change A’s temperature and salinity, then play separation. B stays at 15°C and SP 34. Cold, fresher seawater can still be lighter.
water.diagram: Fixed section of two continuous water bodies. Warm-brown circles track A; light diamonds track B. The same marks undergo a reversible geometric rearrangement showing density order, not a fluid-dynamics solution.
water.reference: B stays at 15°C and practical salinity 34. Compare equal volumes at the same pressure.
water.saltNote: “Fresher” here still means seawater. SP is practical salinity; 35 roughly corresponds to 35 grams of salt per kilogram of seawater, not an exact conversion.
water.progressNote: Playback reveals relative positions in seven display seconds and supports pause and rewind. It is not a flow field or actual speed. Circles and diamonds track the same water bodies, not molecules; heat and salt diffusion are not simulated.
water.rise: A is less dense and tends to remain above B. Try cooling A: with less salt, it can still be less dense.
water.sink: A is denser and tends to sink below B. Cooling and added salt can both increase seawater density.
water.neutral: A and B have similar densities at this display’s resolution. No distinct density layering is shown here.
water.globalTitle: Why are ocean currents more than one conveyor?
water.globalIntro: Local density differences can make water sink, but cannot explain global currents alone. Trace the surface, deep and return pathways.
water.globalDiagram: Mechanism diagram linking ocean basins: wind-driven surface circulation, sinking in some high-latitude regions, branching deep exchanges, and wind and mixing helping water return upward.
water.deep: Deep: sinking dense water and exchange
water.globalNote: An original mechanism diagram, not live currents, exact routes or a speed forecast. The ocean has many pathways, not one conveyor belt.
water.bridge: Local density differences are one part of ocean circulation. Continue with atmosphere, day and night, or other connected Earth questions.
water.deepTitle: How can equal volumes have different masses?
water.deepText: Density is mass per unit volume. Within this seawater range, cooling generally increases density, and adding salt also increases it. The effects can reinforce or offset each other. Real water columns also involve pressure, mixing, winds and topography. Fresh water’s low-temperature anomaly is outside these controls.
water.model: Readouts use the EOS-80 surface-pressure equation for 5–25°C and practical salinity 30–38, displayed to 0.1 kg/m³. This is a limited teaching comparison; modern oceanography uses TEOS-10. Positions are not a fluid-dynamics solution; heat and salt diffusion are not simulated. Density differences below 0.05 kg/m³ lie in the display-resolution band.
water.sectionNote: Fixed section · Colors and symbols track origin. The dashed boundary is not a divider or a map of real water color or temperature.

sky.question: One Earth: why do day and night change, and why do auroras glow?
sky.hint: Move solar time and follow the equatorial site EQ-A through one turn. Then reveal the solar wind, magnetic field and aurora layers.
sky.timeNote: View from above the North Pole; equinox case and one fixed equatorial site. Solar time is not civil clock time. Refraction and twilight are omitted.
sky.daynightDiagram: Day and night viewed from above the North Pole. Sunlight arrives from the left and EQ-A rotates around the equator.
sky.day: EQ-A is on the daylight side
sky.night: EQ-A is on the night side
sky.horizon: EQ-A is at the geometric terminator
sky.north: View from above the North Pole
sky.spaceDiagram: Near-Earth space section: the magnetosphere is compressed sunward and stretched into a tail away from the Sun. Energetic particles reach the polar upper atmosphere along magnetic field lines, producing auroras.
sky.aurora: Auroras in the polar upper atmosphere
sky.layerNote: Switches reveal drawings. They do not switch off the solar wind, Earth’s actual field or its atmosphere.
sky.scale: Different viewpoints: Earth, magnetosphere and auroral-layer thickness do not share a scale.
sky.explain: Rotation turns the site toward and away from the Sun, making day and night. Auroras follow another chain: solar wind couples to the magnetosphere; particles gain energy and enter the polar upper atmosphere, where collisions make gases glow.
sky.dayAurora: Auroras also happen in daytime. A dark sky makes visible auroras easier to see. The terminator does not cause auroras, and the equatorial site is not an aurora observing site.
sky.bridge: Sunlight, oceans and the space environment each have their own mechanisms. When they interact, can one switch tell us whether Earth is habitable?
sky.deepTitle: Photons and charged particles are different
sky.deepText: Sunlight carries radiant energy; the solar wind is flowing plasma. Earth’s magnetic field redirects charged particles. It is not a solid shell that blocks every kind of radiation. Some particles and energy still enter the magnetosphere; particles accelerated there can excite the upper atmosphere. This locates mechanisms, not current space weather or an aurora forecast.

conditions.question: If one condition changes, how far can we reason?
conditions.hint: Follow energy input, air and water, then long-term change. Separate a supported direction of change from the conditions still missing.
conditions.unknown: What this alone cannot tell us
conditions.irradiance: Sunlight on a unit area facing the Sun, above the atmosphere
conditions.formula: Relative sunlight = 1/r². Solar luminosity stays fixed; compare unit areas facing the Sun above the atmosphere. This is not surface temperature or a habitability test.
conditions.diagram: Proportional bars compare reference sunlight with sunlight at the selected distance. Reference is one.
conditions.thread: Energy received → air retains and oceans redistribute → gravity, rocks and moons affect long-term evolution
conditions.closing: A home for life is more than a checklist. Distance, air, oceans, rocks and stellar activity interact. Here we compare mechanisms, without assigning Earth a habitability score.

orbit.name: Distance and energy
orbit.ask: If Earth were 5% closer to the Sun, would all its oceans certainly evaporate?
orbit.robust: For the same Sun, moving to 0.95 AU increases sunlight per unit area by about 10.8%.
orbit.unknown: This step alone cannot tell us the warming or whether every ocean evaporates. We also need cloud and ice reflectivity, greenhouse effects, ocean heat storage and transport, and duration.
orbit.evidence: Light spreads over a larger area as it travels outward; irradiance follows the inverse square of distance. The climate response to changed energy also involves feedbacks.
orbit.connection: The water page changes local temperature and salt. This changes energy input; its slider cannot directly set global ocean temperature.

atmosphere.name: Air and warmth
atmosphere.ask: With a weaker greenhouse effect, would Earth still receive sunlight?
atmosphere.robust: Sunlight still brings energy. With other conditions held equal, a weaker greenhouse effect means a cooler surface. The effect operates by day and by night.
atmosphere.unknown: One “air on/off” switch cannot calculate temperature. Composition, pressure, clouds and water vapor all affect the energy balance. A natural greenhouse effect does not mean stronger is always better.
atmosphere.evidence: NASA’s energy-budget and greenhouse resources distinguish incoming sunlight from outgoing thermal radiation. Water vapor also changes with temperature, creating feedback.
atmosphere.connection: The day/night drawing tells us whether the site faces the Sun. Night does not turn off the greenhouse effect.

gravity.name: Mass and gravity
gravity.ask: If Earth had 20% less mass, would it quickly lose its water?
gravity.robust: If radius were held fixed, lower mass would weaken surface gravity. Gravity affects the energy atmospheric particles need to escape.
gravity.unknown: “20% less” alone gives no water-loss rate. Radius, atmospheric composition and temperature, solar ultraviolet radiation, replenishment and history also matter. Changing mass may change radius too.
gravity.evidence: ESA’s Mars–Venus comparison finds that gravity and solar ultraviolet radiation both affect ion escape. Magnetic fields cannot explain every difference between the planets.
gravity.connection: Density, mass and volume are related. A local water-density comparison is not a planetary atmospheric-escape model.

interior.name: Interior heat and rocks
interior.ask: As Earth’s interior cools, will it lose its oceans tomorrow?
interior.robust: Internal heat helps drive plate motion and volcanism. Exchanges among rocks, oceans and air influence the long-term environment.
interior.unknown: Less internal heat cannot directly give tomorrow’s temperature or a deadline for ocean loss. Rock evolution takes long periods; this does not establish plate tectonics as necessary for all life.
interior.evidence: USGS distinguishes heat left from formation and heat from radioactive decay. Direct volcanic heat is small beside solar input; rock cycling also involves long-term carbon exchange.
interior.connection: Currents redistribute heat already in the ocean. Heat-driven rock changes belong to a different timescale.

moon.name: The Moon and long-term change
moon.ask: Without the Moon, would Earth certainly be uninhabitable?
moon.robust: The Moon contributes to tides and constrains long-term variation in Earth’s axial tilt.
moon.unknown: This does not establish that every moonless planet is uninhabitable. A moonless Earth’s tilt also depends on initial spin and perturbations from other planets. Studies find different ranges under different assumptions.
moon.evidence: NASA’s Earth resources describe the Moon’s effect on tilt. Numerical moonless-Earth research archived by NASA tests different initial conditions; these are not observations of suddenly removing the Moon.
moon.connection: Earth’s rotation creates day and night. The Moon does not cast Earth’s nightly darkness.

magnetic.name: Magnetism and space
magnetic.ask: Without a global intrinsic magnetic field, must all the air be stripped away?
magnetic.robust: Earth’s field changes charged solar-wind particle paths and participates in auroras and some escape processes.
magnetic.unknown: A magnetic field is not an atmosphere switch. Venus has no Earth-like global intrinsic field but retains thick air. Gravity, ultraviolet heating, composition, replenishment and history also matter.
magnetic.evidence: ESA’s Earth, Mars and Venus comparisons show that magnetic shielding and atmospheric retention do not have a one-to-one relationship. An ionosphere can also form an induced magnetosphere with the solar wind.
magnetic.connection: Hiding the field layer changes the drawing. It does not simulate atmospheric loss after removing the field.
